% Numerical tables for the QT section.
% Generated by:  python -m autext.qt.tables base --latex
%                python -m autext.qt.tables lift <ref36-dir> --latex
%                python -m autext.qt.tables lrc
% Raw runs: results/run/table_base.log, table_lift.log, table_lrc.log
%
% Local codes are those passing Ref. [36]'s qLDPC criterion: the dual has
% identical parameters, and the generator weight w >= 6 (w = 4 is toric-like).
%
% NOTE on Table 2's source.  Its rows are Ref. [36]'s ANCILLARY parity-check
% matrices (the arXiv source archive), not its printed Table 1 -- those two
% disagree, see the footnotes and results/tables.log.  The matrices are the
% right source here because they are what was actually scheduled: n and k below
% are computed from them, not read off a filename or a table.
%
% NOTE on t_LR.  This is the AMORTIZED cost of the left-right circuit of
% Ref. [24]: their t_1 + t_2, with the initialisation and measurement rounds
% excluded, so it is like-for-like with a CNOT depth.  It is searched over
% partitions of the BASE graph -- a base partition lifts to the full code with
% the same t_1 + t_2, and the base graph is small enough that the search reaches
% the optimum, where the same search over all lifted qubits gets stuck two
% layers worse on [[144,12,11]].  t_LR >= Delta for every partition, so an
% interleaved circuit of depth Delta can be matched but never beaten; see
% autext/qt/lrc.py for the proof.

\caption{The reduced problem, the two solvers on it, and the left-right
comparison. Every pair of local codes passing Ref.~[36]'s qLDPC criterion, swept
over all inequivalent column permutations of the index-1 matrices $H_1, H_1'$
(30 each for $[6,3,3]$ and $[8,4,4]$, 3 for $[4,2,2]$, 1 for $[2,1,2]$). The
base graph depends only on the local codes and this permutation, never on the
group $G$ or the multisets $\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}$, so one row covers every
lifted code built from that pair. BOTH solvers are run on EVERY class, so the
columns separate three outcomes --- the greedy of Box~1 reaches $\Delta$; it
misses but CP-SAT reaches $\Delta$; or CP-SAT \emph{proves} $\Delta$ infeasible
on every straddling halving --- and the two time columns compare the methods
rather than one against the other's leftovers. Wherever the greedy succeeds
CP-SAT independently confirms feasibility (no disagreements in 3180 classes).
Totals: 3136 greedy, 20 CP-SAT-only, 24 certified infeasible, 0 unresolved;
$371$\,s of greedy against $3239$\,s of CP-SAT, a gap that grows with the base
graph from parity at 72--256 edges to $11.5\times$ at 576. $t_{\rm LR}$ is the
range, over the same classes, of the amortized left-right cost of Ref.~[24]; it
equals $\Delta$ on only 240 of the 3180 classes, and never once $w\geq9$ (0 of
1800). $[8,4,4]\times[8,4,4]$ ($w=16$, $\Delta=20$) is outside the weight
window.}
\label{tab:qt-base}

\caption{Every quantum Tanner code of Ref.~[36], scheduled directly from its
published parity-check matrices. $n$ and $k$ are computed from those matrices;
$d_{\rm est}$ is Ref.~[36]'s QDistRnd estimate, an upper bound rather than a
proven distance. $\Delta$ is the K\"onig lower bound of Eq.~(3);
$\Delta_X{+}\Delta_Z$ is the alternating circuit; $t_{\rm LR}$ is the amortized
cost of the left-right circuit of Ref.~[24] (their $t_1+t_2$, with the
initialisation and measurement rounds excluded so that it is like-for-like with
a CNOT depth); the last column is the depth our circuit attains. All our
circuits are proper and contamination-free, checked by the Eq.~(2) parity
formula and by an independent propagation simulation. We match or beat
$t_{\rm LR}$ on every one of the 27 codes and strictly beat it on 21, by up to
4 layers; 25 of the 27 attain $\Delta$.
$^\dagger$~These two attain only $\Delta+1$: a depth-$(\Delta+1)$ circuit
certifies the orientation, and CP-SAT then proves depth $\Delta$ infeasible for
that orientation on every balanced halving; generic CP-SAT with no sandwich
constraint also reaches only $7$ on both. The left-right circuit needs $7$ there
as well, so it does not overtake us.
$^\ddagger$~Present in Ref.~[36]'s ancillary files but not in its printed
Table~1, which instead lists $[[112,2,12]]$ and $[[144,2,14]]$ in the $w=8$
block --- no matrices are shipped for those two, so they cannot be scheduled
here.
$^\S$~The file is named \texttt{252\_2\_20} and Ref.~[36]'s Table~1 reports
$k=2$, but the shipped matrix has $\mathrm{rank}\,H_X=\mathrm{rank}\,H_Z=124$
and hence $k=252-248=4$ (confirmed three ways; the other 26 files all match
their labels).}
\label{tab:qt-lift}
\end{table}
